name: issue_827_off_day_floor_breach_escalates
description: Issue #827 GAP-1 / #1066 (Design D nearest-edge arming, docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md section 6f). An off-classified day (mild day type, classifier hvac_mode=off) gets the same floor defense as every other day type: indoor decays from 73F (cooling zone) to 64F, 4F below the 68F floor, and the first evaluation below the floor (08:30) arms heat and commands it. Before #827 an off day had no floor defense at all; before #1066 it needed a mild-tier deadband plus a 90 s sustain.
source: Issue #827 Design table, GAP-1 — off-classified days previously had no floor defense whatsoever.
notes: Occupant impact: on a mild day forecast as 'HVAC off' a cold snap or overnight drift must still be corrected. The house must get heat on the first evaluation below the floor, not drift arbitrarily cold.

Design D rule exercised (docs/08 section 6f): indoor < floor -> heating immediately on any day type. The 08:32 re-evaluation is a redundant re-affirmation kept from the original timing; the final-state assertions at 08:32 cannot prove WHEN heating was armed (comfort_family reads final state). Timing evidence: issue_1066_cold_morning_mild_day_arms_heat_immediately.json. Near-duplicate of issue_821_comfort_floor_fallback_no_confidence.json (mild vs warm, 64F vs 67F) and issue_827_missing_forecast_fallback_escalates.json.

Baseline fix (Issue #1066 review): the original baseline sat inside the heat zone (indoor <= floor + m), so heat was already armed before the breach and the final-state assertions passed vacuously. The baseline is now inside the cooling zone so the breach reading is the first thing that can arm heat. (70F at baseline equals floor + m, which is the inclusive heat zone, so heat was already armed at 08:00.)

(a) Scenario effectiveness: with nearest-edge arming deleted (origin/main) a mild day is natively neither family; heat is against-grain, needs the mild-tier deadband (2F) cleared plus a recency check and a 90 s sustain across two evaluations. If a regression re-excluded mild/off days from floor defense entirely (the pre-#827 GAP-1), comfort_family would stay cooling and the final assertions fail.
(b) Docs<->production alignment: docs/08 section 6f ('The day type is not an input to the arming decision'; 'indoor < floor -> heating').
(c) Occupant outcome if this test fails to catch a regression: the home drifts arbitrarily cold overnight or in a cold snap on a day forecast as mild, with zero corrective heating.
Classification fields: windows_recommended=true and hvac_mode=off match DayClassification._compute_recommendations()'s real DAY_TYPE_MILD branch (classifier.py).

events.note: Mild-day classification (hvac_mode=off, windows_recommended=true as classifier.py derives for DAY_TYPE_MILD). Indoor 70F is within the band [68F, 74F].
Baseline: indoor 73F, inside the band [68F, 74F] and in the cooling zone (>= 74 - 2): cool is armed at 74. No breach.
Indoor has decayed to 64F, 4F below comfort_heat(68).
First evaluation with indoor below the floor: floor breach, heat is armed immediately and commanded at comfort_heat.
Re-evaluation 2 minutes later: still below the floor, heating remains armed (redundant re-affirmation kept from the original timeline).

assertions.reason: Baseline: mild day, indoor within band — comfort band arms normally.
GAP-1 fix: an off/mild-classified day gets real floor defense. Final-state assertion (reads the engine's final state); heating was armed at the first below-floor evaluation, 08:30.
The escalated mode is a real climate.set_temperature/set_hvac_mode call at comfort_heat, not merely an internal flag.

verdict.summary: An off/mild-classified day, which previously had zero comfort-floor defense, arms heat on the first evaluation below the floor.
verdict.observed_behavior: Cooling family at 70F (in-band); the 64F reading at 08:30 arms heating, and heat is commanded at comfort_heat.
verdict.expected_behavior: Every day type, including mild/off, has the same nearest-edge floor defense (docs/08 section 6f).
